# cycle_tls_certificate (Resource)

Uploads a user-supplied TLS certificate (`POST /v1/dns/tls/user-certificates`). There is no update endpoint; changing `bundle` or `private_key` forces replacement.

Cycle has no hard delete. Destroy issues a `deprecate` job so the platform can fall back to another certificate (or generate one) for the applicable domains.

After import, `bundle` and `private_key` are unset because the API does not return private material. Set them in configuration and ignore them on `ImportStateVerify`.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Upload a user-supplied certificate. Cycle has no hard delete — destroy
# issues a deprecate job so the platform can fall back to another cert.
resource "cycle_tls_certificate" "custom" {
  bundle      = file("${path.module}/cert.pem")
  private_key = file("${path.module}/key.pem")
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `bundle` (String, Sensitive) PEM-encoded certificate bundle. Changing this forces a new certificate to be uploaded.
- `private_key` (String, Sensitive) The certificate's private key. Changing this forces a new certificate to be uploaded.

### Read-Only

- `domains` (List of String) Domains associated with the certificate.
- `expires` (String) Expiration timestamp of the certificate, as RFC3339.
- `hub_id` (String) The ID of the hub this certificate belongs to.
- `id` (String) The unique ID of the TLS certificate.
- `state` (String) The current state of the certificate (e.g. `live`, `new`, `processing`).
- `user_supplied` (Boolean) Whether this certificate was uploaded instead of generated by the platform.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Certificates are imported using their ID. bundle and private_key are
# not returned by the API and must be set in configuration after import.
terraform import cycle_tls_certificate.custom 651efd54c53f7b6e2c5a9f21
```
